reproduction_target: Computational half of a wet-lab-anchored study: bulk RNA-Seq of TGFb-treated vs untreated GM05386 primary human skin fibroblasts, analysed as (a) a differential-gene-expression arm (Trimmomatic -> FastQC -> kallisto against a gffread-built GRCh38/Ensembl-109 transcriptome -> tximport -> DESeq2 -> ShinyGO functional enrichment) and (b) two orthogonal alternative-splicing arms — the in-house 'RNomic UdeS' pipeline (Bowtie 2 -> RSEM -> event-based PSI with BH-adjusted Fisher exact test) and rMATS (Trimmomatic -> STAR -> samtools -> rMATS with stated FDR/TPM/dPSI filters). The same pipelines are re-run on three public GEO datasets (GSE110021, GSE252425, GSE264038). Reproduction target = Tables S1-S5 and Figs 2, 3, 5A, 6. Cell culture, TGFb stimulation, RNA extraction, library prep/sequencing, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, AS-PCR and ddPCR are wet-lab (W, OOS for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, derived from the bioRxiv JATS XML full text (fetched by curl; WebFetch returned HTTP 403). The paper states NO code repository of any kind (no GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo/Software Heritage URL, no 'Code availability' section), so there is no landing page or README prose to read and no workflow file to anchor granularity on. The three splicing/expression arms share the Trimmomatic/FastQC front end; it is counted once (C1, C2) and referenced by both DESeq2 and rMATS arms. The in-house 'RNomic UdeS' pipeline is counted as three steps (Bowtie 2 alignment, RSEM quantification, PSI/ASE computation + statistics) because those are the named invocations in prose.

steps.label: Read trimming with Trimmomatic V0.39 (own FASTQ + GSE110021/GSE252425/GSE264038); no trimming parameters/adapter file stated
Read-quality assessment with FastQC V0.11.9 (QC only; defaults implied, no parameters stated)
Transcriptome FASTA construction with gffread (cufflinks V2.2.1) from the Ensembl GRCh38 genome + annotation V109; no gffread flags stated
Transcript pseudo-alignment and quantification with kallisto V0.48.0 against the GRCh38/Ensembl-109 transcriptome; no index or quant flags (bootstrap count, fragment length, strandedness) stated
Gene-level summarisation of kallisto estimates with the tximport package V1.22.0; countsFromAbundance/tx2gene construction not stated

Differential gene expression with DESeq2 V1.34, default Benjamini-Hochberg correction (Tables S1, S5); design formula, independent-filtering and shrinkage settings not stated, significance cut-offs only shown inside Fig. 2A

Functional enrichment (GO biological process / molecular function / cellular component, KEGG) of the 453 up-regulated genes with ShinyGO 0.77 (web service); no background gene set, FDR cut-off, pathway-size limits or underlying gene-set release stated

RNomic UdeS pipeline: read alignment with Bowtie 2 V2.4.4 to 'the curated version 109 of the UCSC reference transcriptome (hg38)'; the curated reference is in-house and not distributed, and no bowtie2 flags are stated
RNomic UdeS pipeline: per-isoform TPM quantification with RSEM V1.3.3; no RSEM flags or strandedness stated

RNomic UdeS pipeline: in-house alternative-splicing-event identification and PSI computation (long/short form ratio) with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted exact Fisher test (Tables S3, S4); the pipeline itself is unpublished in-house code with no version, no repository, and its 'more stringent threshold' is never numerically specified
rMATS arm: alignment of trimmed reads to the human reference genome GRCh38 (Ensembl release 109) with STAR v2.7.10a 'with default parameters'
rMATS arm: retention of primary alignments with Samtools v1.16.1; the exact filtering command/flags are not stated

rMATS arm: differential alternative splicing with rMATS v4.1.2 on STAR-aligned reads, filtered to FDR < 0.05, at least one TPM in each sample, and |inclusion level difference| > 0.1 (Table S2); read-length/paired-end and --novelSS settings not stated

headline.static_readiness: 0/13 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 1/13 computational steps (C3, the gffread transcriptome build, whose only input is the public Ensembl GRCh38 v109 genome+annotation). The other 12/13 steps cap at NI, driven by two independent zeros: (i) the study's own RNA-Seq raw data has no accession — Methods say only 'deposit as GEO dataset (pending)' — so every step consuming this study's FASTQ scores data=0; (ii) the in-house RNomic UdeS splicing pipeline (C10) is unpublished code with no version and an unspecified stringency threshold, scoring code=0 and version=0. No code repository of any kind is stated anywhere in the paper, so all analysis code is at best reconstructable from prose. No lockfile, container or conda environment is claimed; tool pins are scattered exact versions in prose only (Trimmomatic V0.39, FastQC V0.11.9, kallisto V0.48.0, cufflinks V2.2.1, tximport V1.22.0, DESeq2 V1.34, ShinyGO 0.77, Bowtie 2 V2.4.4, RSEM V1.3.3, STAR v2.7.10a, Samtools v1.16.1, rMATS v4.1.2), i.e. exact_pins_partial with no environment closure. Even a Stage-2 code check could not raise any step above RI while no environment capture exists and no repository is published.
headline.coverage: 13 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full-text Methods prose. 7 wet-lab steps (cell culture/maintenance of GM05386 fibroblasts, TGFb differentiation, RNA extraction + qRT-PCR, RNA-Seq library prep and NovaSeq sequencing, immunofluorescence + ImageJ quantification, AS-PCR + LabChip electrophoresis, ddPCR on the Bio-Rad QX200) counted in W but out of computational-reproduction scope. Computational coverage = 13/20.

gaps.where: Whole paper — there is no 'Code availability' section
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked anywhere: no GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage URL appears in the Methods, Acknowledgement, Author Contribution or supplemental table legends. The DESeq2 arm, the rMATS arm and the RNomic UdeS arm are described in prose only; no scripts, parameter files or figure-generation code exist for a reproducer.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the DESeq2/rMATS/UdeS driver scripts and figure code in a public repository with an archived (Zenodo DOI) snapshot, and cite it in a Code availability statement.

gaps.where: This study's own RNA-Seq raw data (Methods, 'RNA-Seq library preparation and sequencing')
gaps.missing: The only statement is 'Sequencing was performed on Illumina NovaSeq by Genome Quebec deposit as GEO dataset (pending)' — no GEO/SRA/ArrayExpress accession number, no sample-to-file mapping, no per-replicate metadata for the three biological replicates of treated vs untreated GM05386 fibroblasts. The primary result set (Tables S1-S3, Figs 2-5) therefore has no retrievable input data.
gaps.how_to_close: Complete the GEO deposition and publish the GSE accession with a sample table mapping each FASTQ to condition and biological replicate.

gaps.missing: The 'in-house' UdeS pipeline is not public. It is only described narratively (Bowtie 2 -> RSEM -> long/short-form PSI -> BH-adjusted exact Fisher test) with a citation to a prior paper (Armero et al. 2017 / Cloutier et al. 2018) and 'with minor modifications'. The modifications are not enumerated and the 'more stringent threshold' that produced 8 significant ASEs out of 30,002 is never given numerically.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the pipeline (or the exact version used) with its event-definition rules, the significance/dPSI thresholds actually applied, and the list of modifications relative to the cited prior version.

gaps.where: Bowtie 2 reference for the UdeS arm (C8)
gaps.missing: 'the curated version 109 of the UCSC reference transcriptome (hg38)' is an in-house curated derivative. Neither the curation procedure nor the resulting FASTA/index is distributed or given an accession/checksum, so the alignment reference cannot be rebuilt identically.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the curated transcriptome FASTA (or the script + source files + checksum that generate it) alongside the pipeline.

gaps.missing: The UdeS pipeline carries no version identifier at all (version=0). ShinyGO 0.77 is version-pinned but is a hosted web service whose underlying GO/KEGG gene-set release is not recorded, so the enrichment inputs are effectively unversioned even though the front end is pinned.
gaps.how_to_close: Assign and cite a version/commit for the UdeS pipeline; record the GO/KEGG database release date used by ShinyGO, or re-run enrichment locally with a versioned annotation package.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image/digest, conda/mamba environment YAML, renv.lock or session_info is claimed anywhere. Exact versions exist for 12 tools as scattered prose pins, but no interpreter (R version, Python version), no channel/index, and no platform is declared, so there is no environment closure — capture_claim is exact_pins_partial, and version is capped at 1 for every step.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi lockfile or a container digest pinning R + Bioconductor (DESeq2 1.34, tximport 1.22.0), the aligners (Bowtie 2 2.4.4, STAR 2.7.10a), kallisto 0.48.0, RSEM 1.3.3, samtools 1.16.1 and rMATS 4.1.2, together with the declared platform.

gaps.where: Statistical thresholds for the DESeq2 arm (C6)
gaps.missing: The significance cut-offs used to call 453 up- and 1,998 down-regulated genes out of 18,910 are stated only as 'cut-off parameters' inside the Fig. 2A schematic, not in the Methods prose; the DESeq2 design formula and filtering settings are absent.
gaps.how_to_close: State the log2FC and adjusted-p thresholds, the design formula, and any pre-filtering in Methods.

gaps.missing: Cell culture/maintenance of GM05386 primary skin fibroblasts, TGFb differentiation, RNA extraction + qRT-PCR, RNA-Seq library preparation and NovaSeq sequencing, immunofluorescence with ImageJ quantification, AS-PCR + LabChip electrophoresis, and ddPCR on the Bio-Rad QX200 are physical steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the reproducible computational entry point would be the (pending) GEO FASTQ deposition.
